claims.text: Correct or exclude other Eti of anemia first; after starting and after each dose Δ, check Hb wkly until stable.
claims.quote: Correct or exclude other causes of anemia (e.g., vitamin deficiency, metabolic or chronic inflammatory conditions, bleeding, etc.) before initiating Epogen. Following initiation of therapy and after each dose adjustment, monitor hemoglobin weekly until the hemoglobin level is stable and sufficient to minimize the need for RBC transfusion.

claims.text: CI: PRCA that began after any EPO product;
claims.quote: Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) that begins after treatment with Epogen or other erythropoietin protein drugs ( 4 )

claims.text: multidose vials (benzyl alcohol) in neonates, infants, preg or lactating women.
claims.quote: Use of the multiple-dose vials containing benzyl alcohol in neonates, infants, pregnant women, and lactating women ( 4 )

claims.text: Raises sz risk in CKD: monitor closely for premonitory neuro Sx during the first several months.
claims.quote: Epogen increases the risk of seizures in patients with CKD. During the first several months following initiation of Epogen, monitor patients closely for premonitory neurologic symptoms.

claims.text: Serious allergic rxns (anaphylaxis, angioedema, bronchospasm): stop it permanently.
claims.quote: Serious allergic reactions, including anaphylactic reactions, angioedema, bronchospasm, skin rash, and urticaria may occur with Epogen. Immediately and permanently discontinue Epogen and administer appropriate therapy if a serious allergic or anaphylactic reaction occurs.

Blistering and skin exfoliation reactions including Erythema multiforme and Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), have been reported in patients treated with ESAs (including Epogen) in the postmarketing setting. Discontinue Epogen therapy immediately if a severe cutaneous reaction, such as SJS/TEN, is suspected.

claims.text: Poor or lost Hb response: look for Fe deficiency, infect, inflam or bleed, then PRCA.
claims.quote: For lack or loss of hemoglobin response to Epogen, initiate a search for causative factors (e.g., iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, bleeding). If typical causes of lack or loss of hemoglobin response are excluded, evaluate for PRCA
claims.locator: 5.5 Lack or Loss of Hemoglobin Response to Epogen

claims.text: Severe anemia w a ↓retic count: withhold it and test for neutralizing antibodies.
claims.quote: If severe anemia and low reticulocyte count develop during treatment with Epogen, withhold Epogen and evaluate patients for neutralizing antibodies to erythropoietin.

claims.text: PRCA: stop permanently and don't switch to another ESA.
claims.quote: Permanently discontinue Epogen in patients who develop PRCA following treatment with Epogen or other erythropoietin protein drugs. Do not switch patients to other ESAs.
